course_name_original: Gestión de la Cadena de Suministro
prerequisites: Completion of all first-year courses of the Master's Degree in Industrial Engineering is recommended, as the course will use concepts and techniques from those courses and undergraduate studies.
Basic knowledge of English (B1 level) is recommended for understanding additional materials and using computer programs.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the importance of supply chain management in a globalized market and the use of its key control elements.

Know how to design a supply chain, distinguishing the role played by each link or part of the supply chain in achieving customer satisfaction and performing comprehensive operations planning that allows for the supply of products to the end customer.
Make decisions about procurement management and proper product storage.
Know how to coordinate the activities of suppliers and customers within the supply chain and its impact on the effectiveness and efficiency of the chain.
Understand the application of information technologies and apply tools that allow the resolution of problems related to supply chain management, putting acquired knowledge into practice.

syllabus_topics: General Overview of the Supply Chain
Supply chain management and decision areas
Key properties: Efficiency, flexibility, and resilience
Trends: Global, circular, and digital supply chains
Risk management in the supply chain
The Ripple Effect in the supply chain
Key concepts: Strategic design and operational design
Analysis of efficiency, flexibility, and resilience
The Bullwhip Effect in the supply chain
Multi-echelon management: Push, pull, and the decoupling point
The European Union framework in Circular Economy and waste management
Challenges in implementing supply chains compatible with the Circular Economy
teaching_methods: Classroom practices (numerical exercises and case studies)

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment activities (individual and team assignments, projects, oral tests)
Final exam (written test with theoretical questions, numerical exercises, and practical cases)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as 0.6 * Continuous Assessment Activities + 0.4 * Final Exam. A minimum total score of 5 points is required to pass the subject. This method requires attendance at a minimum of 75% of scheduled contact hours. For extraordinary calls and differentiated evaluation, the final grade is calculated as 0.4 * Assignments and Projects + 0.6 * Final Exam, and a minimum total score of 5 points is also required. This system also applies to students who do not meet the 75% attendance minimum in the ordinary call.
